title: Time-slice KPI lab — personal OKR draft
body:
Context:
I want a compact, repeatable way to evaluate personal contribution impact on the product and my development velocity without making OKRs feel like a checklist. This is an experiment to combine time-slicing (blocks of focus), throughput metrics, and a subjective quality signal into a weekly micro-OKR that can be iterated on.

Why this form factor:
- short weekly slices make it easy to pivot experiments and signal changes quickly
- mix of objective (PR lead time, merged features) and subjective (focus score, disruption index) metrics
- aim for a lightweight retrospective at the end of the slice that feeds the next slice's hypothesis

Objective (draft):
- O: Increase net engineering impact per week while maintaining code quality and reducing context-switch overhead.

Key Results (candidate KRs for the quarter):
- KR1: Raise average weekly merged story points from 6 -> 9 (tracking via GH labels + small point estimate)
- KR2: Reduce median PR review turnaround time from 36h -> 18h for my authored PRs
- KR3: Maintain a personal focus score >= 3.5/5 on at least 8 of 10 weeks (see focus metric below)
- KR4: Keep post-release bug rate (1-week window) for my changes <= 3% of deployed lines (approx)

Definitions / Metrics (how I'll measure things):
- Focus blocks: 90-min blocks scheduled in calendar, counted if 70% of block was uninterrupted (no meeting >10 min, no Slack pings > 3)
- Focus score (0-5): self-rated after each day (0 total churned day -> 5 deep flow all day); weekly average is used for KR3
- Throughput: merged story points + number of meaningful small PRs (<= 300 LOC) merged
- PR lead time: time from PR open -> merged (exclude WIP labels)
- Disruption index: count of ad-hoc interrupts in a week (pull requests requesting review outside scheduled times, urgent meetings)
- Quality: number of bugs reported in the first week after deployment attributable to my changes (tracked by labeling in tickets)

Weekly slice template (what I fill out each week):
- Week range: YYYY-MM-DD -> YYYY-MM-DD
- Hypothesis for this week: (one-line experiment)
- Planned focus blocks: N blocks (list quick themes: e.g., "quantize batching experiments, batch client API", "docs and runbook for model pinning")
- Hard commitments (no-escape): 2 story-pinned items (quick descriptors + estimate)
- Metrics baseline at start of week: focus score, open PRs, expected merges, planned meetings
- Outcome at end of week: merged points, PR lead time median, focus score average, disruptions, post-release issues
- Retro notes: what worked, what blocked, immediate changes for next week

Example filled slice (Week 2026-02-16 -> 2026-02-22):
- Hypothesis: Time-boxing API work into morning deep blocks + review blocks in afternoon reduces PR lead time and increases merged points.
- Planned focus blocks: 6 (API refactor, batching metrics, two small production fixes)
- Hard commitments: finish API doc + ship batching telemetry dashboard (3 pts), finalize PR for model-fallback policy (2 pts)
- Baseline: focus score 3.2 (prev week), 4 open PRs, scheduled 5 meetings
- Outcome: merged points = 7, median PR lead time = 22h, focus score average = 3.8, disruptions = 2 (urgent infra incident), bugs in first week = 1
- Retro: deep blocks helped reduce fragmentation; afternoon review windows improved PR lead time; infra incident derailed two blocks -> consider moving one block later in day to avoid ops overlap

Mini retrospective learnings so far (Nov 2025 -> Mar 2026 rolling):
- Pattern: mornings are consistently better for deep work; late afternoons are risky because of cross-org syncs.
- Scheduling explicit review windows (e.g., 2-4pm review) reduced feedback loop noise for my team reviewers.
- Small, clear PRs (<300 LOC) correlate with faster merges and fewer review rounds.
- Focus score correlates with contiguous blocks; when blocks drop below 3 per week my throughput falls ~25%.

Open experiments to try next quarter:
- Experiment A: 2-week focused sprint (4 days of deep blocks, 1 day for catch-up/review) vs. normal cadence. Measure delta in merged points and bug rate.
- Experiment B: Auto-reschedule one daily block to mid-day when there are >3 meetings on calendar to test resilience to interruptions.
- Experiment C: Pair-review hour once per week to speed-first review of complex PRs and cross-train reviewer context.

Risks and tradeoffs:
- Emphasizing merged points could encourage shipping smaller, less ambitious chunks; mitigate by keeping at least one high-scope item per sprint.
- Self-reported focus score is noisy; complement with objective measurements (calendar vs. activity) but preserve privacy and avoid overinstrumentation.

Next actions (this week):
- Formalize KR tracking in a small spreadsheet (columns: week, merged pts, median PR lead, focus score, disruptions, bugs) — prototype sheet linked in artifacts.
- Add labels in GitHub and JIRA to make it easier to attribute merged points to myself.
- Try Experiment B next week and note changes in the weekly slice template.

Questions for collaborators / manager:
- Does this form and cadence look reasonable for performance review context? (I want to use this for personal improvement, not formal evaluation unless we agree)
- Any suggestions for safe objective metrics to pair with my focus score that won't feel invasive?

Notes to self:
- Keep the weekly slice under 15 minutes to fill out; it's a tool to iterate, not to create paperwork.
- When tracking merged points, be conservative with story point inflation — prefer consistent small estimates rather than optimistic ones.

Misc links (scratch):
- Quick spreadsheet prototype: (to be created)
- Related team playbook: confluence: /display/ENG/weekly-sprint-checks (placeholder)

---
End of draft.

(If this format proves useful after a month, I will try an anonymized summary to share as a productivity pattern for the team.)
